rules.classification: Spectroscopic classes and alert or messenger labels are different definitions and are not compared; two active classes differ when neither label refines the other (for example 'SN Ia' and 'SN Ia-91T' agree); an earlier value from the same provider is a revision.
rules.host: Two proposed hosts agree when their names match after case and spacing are ignored or one name is among the other's NED cross-identifications; otherwise they are an identity ambiguity. Association probabilities are not computed.
rules.photometry: Only exactly compatible photometry (same epoch, band, system, method, calibration and direct/difference state, two or more providers) is compared. The limiting magnitude or flux that a provider reports alongside a detection is that epoch's detection threshold, not a non-detection, and is not compared with the detection; a detection brighter than another provider's non-detection limit at the same epoch is a status conflict. A group is listed only when it is still inconsistent under these rules; at most 10 groups per event, most significant first.
rules.position: Two positions with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they are more than 2 arcsec apart; when one states an error radius, the separation is compared with 3 times that radius.
rules.redshift: Two redshifts with no stated uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 0.005 (about 1,500 km/s); transient and host redshifts are different definitions and are listed, not compared; host redshifts of differently named hosts are an identity ambiguity.
rules.revision: A retracted row, or a superseded row of the same provider whose value differs beyond the property's rule, is a revision or retraction; a revision within the rule is consistent; the earlier value stays visible.
rules.sigma: Two values that both state an uncertainty are inconsistent when they differ by more than 3 combined standard deviations (uncertainties added in quadrature; a stated position error radius is treated as one standard deviation).

evidence_timeline.summary: The exponential growth of large-scale telescope arrays has boosted time-domain astronomy development but introduced operational bottlenecks, including labor-intensive observation planning, data processing, and real-time decision-making. Here we present the StarWhisper Telescope system, an AI agent framework automating end-to-end astronomical observations for surveys like the Nearby Galaxy Supernovae Survey. By integrating large language models with specialized function calls and modular workflows, StarWhisper Telescope autonomously generates site-specific observation lists, executes real-time image analysis via pipelines, and dynamically triggers follow-up proposals upon transient detection. The system reduces human intervention through automated observation planning, telescope controlling and data processing, while enabling seamless collaboration between amateur and professional astronomers. Deployed across Nearby Galaxy Supernovae Survey's network of 10 amateur telescopes, the StarWhisper Telescope has detected transients with promising response times relative to existing surveys. Furthermore, StarWhisper Telescope's scalable agent architecture provides a blueprint for future facilities like the Global Open Transient Telescope Array, where AI-driven autonomy will be critical for managing 60 telescopes.

evidence_timeline.summary: We highlight the fast-rising and red extragalactic transient AT2024advj (ZTF24abxpkhb) found in the ZTF public alert stream. The Fritz science team registered it on the TNS as a young supernova candidate. Our Fastfinder annotator on the Lasair broker flagged its fast-rising nature and red colour. The transient rose at a rate of 1.5 mags per day in the ZTF g-band from forced photometry and is currently bright in the ZTF r-band at m_r = 17.38 +/- 0.04. The source is offset 21.84" N, 22.52" W (10.6 Kpc) from the likely host galaxy UGC 00604, which is at z = 0.017 or d = 70 Mpc (redshift independent, from NED), implying an absolute magnitude of M = -17.1 (assuming m-M = 34.22 and A_r = 0.261). When considering galactic extinction, we measure a colour of g-r = 0.38 +/- 0.06 at the time of discovery.

evidence_timeline.summary: We observed SN 2024advj (ZTF24abxpkhb) using the 40 cm SLT at Lulin Observatory, Taiwan. Our observations confirm that the object is very red, with (g-r) = 0.5. Additionally, we find that the object has brightened rapidly, with g increasing by ~ 4 mag over 2.5 days since the ZTF discovery. The current magnitude is r = 16.60 ± 0.05 mag at MJD 60655.682, corresponding to an absolute magnitude of M_r = -18.13 mag.

The source is offset 21.84" N, 22.52" W (10.6 Kpc) from the likely host galaxy UGC 00604, which is at z = 0.017 or d = 70 Mpc (redshift independent, from NED), implying an absolute magnitude of M = -17.1 (assuming m-M = 34.22 and A_r = 0.261). When considering galactic extinction, we measure a colour of g-r = 0.38 +/- 0.06 at the time of discovery.
